mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a 3-month moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 3-month high-rate period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, signaling labor market strength that supports equity risk appetite and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth rate > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under the trigger are not significantly higher than the 30-day average before the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) of more than 5% in the prior month coincides with a sharp decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST), creating a dual softening that predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -5% AND HOUST monthly change < -3% in the same month
regime_hint: dual softening in supply and demand
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 1-day average during the preceding 30 days (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in manufacturing capacity (INDPRO) above 3% for three consecutive months indicates an over-supplied economy, which typically precedes a sharp S&P 500 drawdown; thus, negative 20-day forward returns are expected when this signal occurs.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the trigger period are not significantly lower than the 10-day average before the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, it suggests a tight labor market that supports accommodative monetary policy, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly average < 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the trigger are not statistically higher than the 30-day average prior to the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure, which historically precedes equity risk aversion and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly average < 2% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during the trigger are not significantly lower than the 30-day average before the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising real yields (implied by FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL < 2%) create a risk-off environment that predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 1-day average during the prior 30 days (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in residential investment (assumed proxy via absence in observable list - use INDPRO as a stand-in) indicated by three consecutive months of flat or negative INDPRO growth predicts a supply shock that drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change <= 0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the trigger are not significantly negative compared to the 30-day pre-trigger average (p > 0.05).
